title: Renters & Home Insurance
description: Your belongings, the building if you own it, and the disasters a standard policy skips.
wolfLine: The landlord insured the walls. You insure what is inside them.

renters-insurance.definition: A policy for a renter’s belongings, their liability, and sometimes a hotel if the place cannot be lived in. The landlord’s policy does not cover the renter’s stuff.
renters-insurance.example: A $192 policy. A fire takes $6,000 of furniture the landlord’s insurance will not replace.

replacement-cost.definition: The insurer pays what it costs to buy a similar item new, minus the deductible, instead of what the old item would sell for.
replacement-cost.example: A stolen laptop costs $1,200 to replace. Replacement cost starts from $1,200, not from a pawn-shop price.

actual-cash-value.definition: Replacement cost minus wear and age. The check is for what the used item was worth, not for a new one.
actual-cash-value.example: That $1,200 laptop is worth $400 used. Actual cash value starts from $400.

lessons.title: Why Renters Need It
lessons.summary: The landlord’s policy covers the building. It does not cover your couch.

steps.context: [[Renters insurance]] covers your belongings and, typically, your [[liability coverage|liability-coverage]]. The landlord’s policy does not.
steps.prompt: Whose policy covers a renter’s furniture after a fire?
choices: The renter’s own policy, if they have one
steps.explain: The landlord insured the building. The couch was yours.

steps.prompt: If you rent, the landlord’s insurance replaces your clothes after a fire.
steps.explain: Their policy is for their building. Your clothes need your policy.

steps.prompt: A guest is hurt in your apartment and sues. Which policy is built for that?
steps.explain: Liability coverage on a renters policy faces that lawsuit.

steps.prompt: A renters policy costs $16 a month. What is that per year?
You own almost nothing expensive. Is that a full reason to skip renters insurance?
choices: No. Liability and a hotel stay can dwarf the value of the couch
Yes. Renters policies only cover jewelry
Yes, because landlords must cover guests
steps.explain: The belongings are only one part. The lawsuit is the other.

lessons.title: What It Covers
lessons.summary: Your things, a lawsuit, and a place to sleep.

steps.context: A typical [[renters insurance]] policy has three jobs: belongings, liability, and extra living costs.
steps.prompt: Which is a usual piece of renters coverage?
choices: A hotel if the apartment cannot be lived in
steps.explain: That hotel piece is often called loss of use. Flood is a different policy.

steps.prompt: The hotel limit is $3,000. Four nights at $150 would be how much?
How much of that $3,000 hotel limit is left after $600?
Renters insurance rebuilds the apartment building.
steps.explain: The building is the landlord’s. Your policy is for you.

steps.prompt: Loss of use helps pay for a ___ if you cannot stay home.
steps.explain: It is shelter, not a shopping spree.

lessons.title: Replacement Cost or Cash Value
lessons.summary: New price, or used price. The policy picks one.

steps.context: [[Replacement cost]] buys a similar new item. [[Actual cash value]] pays the used price.
steps.prompt: What is replacement cost?
choices: What a similar new item costs now
What a used item would sell for
steps.explain: New for old, minus the deductible.

steps.prompt: A laptop costs $1,200 to replace and is worth $400 used. How much more does replacement cost start from?
Replacement cost, $250 deductible. How much do you receive for that laptop?
Actual cash value, same $250 deductible. How much do you receive?
Actual cash value and replacement cost pay the same check.
steps.explain: Age comes out of actual cash value. That is the gap.

lessons.title: Reading the Policy
lessons.summary: Four lines. Know which loss each one answers.

steps.context: Match the loss to the line. A lawsuit is not the belongings limit.

steps.explain: That line says $15,000.

steps.prompt: What is the liability limit?
steps.explain: That line says $100,000.

doc.title: Renters policy

doc.note: Flood is not in this policy.

steps.prompt: The yearly premium is $192. What is that per month?
A guest sues for $40,000. Which line is the one that applies?
steps.explain: A lawsuit is liability. $40,000 is under the $100,000 limit.

steps.prompt: This page includes flood coverage because the note says flood is not in the policy.
steps.explain: The note is the warning. Flood is absent.

lessons.title: Floods and Earthquakes
lessons.summary: The usual policy has a hole where the water and the ground are.

steps.context: An [[exclusion]] is a loss the main policy will not pay. Flood and earthquake are classic ones.
steps.prompt: Usually in a standard home or renters policy, or a separate policy?
items: Wind that tears off roof shingles
steps.explain: Flood and earthquake are the famous holes. Fire, theft, and wind are the usual yes.

steps.prompt: A standard renters policy quietly includes river flood.
steps.explain: Flood is sold separately. The summary will not sneak it in.

steps.prompt: You live where hurricanes push water into streets. What do you ask?
choices: Whether you need a separate flood policy
Whether collision coverage handles a flood
Whether the deductible disappears in a storm
steps.explain: Name the water. Then see if this policy even speaks to it.

steps.prompt: An earthquake policy is separate. Your standard policy excludes earthquakes. The ground shakes and breaks the dishes. What pays?
choices: Only the earthquake policy, if you bought it
The standard policy, because dishes are belongings
steps.explain: The cause is the earthquake. The exclusion follows the cause.

steps.prompt: Flood and earthquake usually need ___ policy.
steps.explain: The main contract stepped aside.

lessons.title: A Home Inventory
lessons.summary: After a fire you will not remember the blender.

steps.title: Write it down before you need it
steps.body:
A home inventory is a list of what you own, with photos and roughly what it cost.

Keep a copy outside the apartment. A list that burns with the couch cannot replace the couch.

steps.prompt: Why make the list before a loss?
choices: After a fire you will not remember every item or its price
The insurer writes the list for you
Lists lower the deductible to zero
steps.explain: Memory is a bad filing cabinet.

steps.prompt: You list a bike at $450, a laptop at $1,200, and a bed at $800. What is the total?
The only copy of the inventory should live in the apartment it describes.
steps.explain: Store a copy somewhere the fire cannot reach.

steps.prompt: What belongs on the list besides the name of the item?
choices: A photo and about what it cost
steps.explain: The photo and the price help the claim. The password helps a thief.

lessons.title: Home Insurance Basics
lessons.summary: Owners insure the building and the things inside it.

steps.context: Home insurance is the owner’s version: the building, the belongings, liability, and often extra living costs.
steps.prompt: How is a home policy different from a renters policy?
choices: It also helps rebuild the building you own
It only covers cars in the driveway
steps.explain: You own the walls, so the policy has to know about the walls.

steps.prompt: Owning a home means flood is included automatically.
steps.explain: Flood is still usually separate. Owning the house does not close that hole.

steps.prompt: A dwelling limit is $250,000. A rebuild estimate is $310,000. How much of the estimate is above the limit?
Why compare the dwelling limit to a rebuild estimate?
choices: The limit, not the sale price, is what the insurer will pay toward rebuilding
The sale price is always the limit
A higher sale price lowers the premium to zero
steps.explain: You insure the cost to rebuild, not the price a buyer would pay for the land.

steps.prompt: The dwelling limit needs to cover the cost to ___, not only the price you paid.
steps.explain: Lumber and labor set that number.

lessons.title: Priya’s Apartment Fire
lessons.summary: The building was the landlord’s. The laptop was hers.

story.title: The night the hallway filled with smoke
story.body:
A fire two floors down fills Priya’s apartment with smoke. She rents. Her landlord’s insurer will look at the building. Her couch, her clothes, and her laptop are hers.

Her renters policy uses replacement cost. Belongings come to **$6,000**. Four hotel nights at **$150** come to **$600**. The deductible is **$500**.

steps.prompt: What do the hotel nights cost?
Belongings plus hotel, before the deductible. What is the total?
After the $500 deductible, how much does the policy pay if both losses are covered?
Why doesn’t the landlord’s policy write that check?
choices: It covers the building, not her belongings
Renters are banned from filing claims
Smoke is an exclusion on every policy
steps.explain: Different owner, different policy.

steps.prompt: She should keep the hotel receipts.
steps.explain: Loss of use is paid from proof, not from memory.
